claims.text: The proposed material is an Mg-based powder mixture containing Nb, Mo, Cr, Al, and Si.
The starting Mg-based powder mixture has a coarse dendritic microstructure.
Residual porosity after powder-metallurgy sintering can deteriorate mechanical properties.
Coarse dendritic microstructures promote phase separation through dendrite-to-interdendrite composition variations.
SPS or HIP at 850–900 °C for 15–30 minutes under vacuum or inert gas is an appropriate processing route for the proposed alloy.
Minor Al and Si additions form a transient liquid through low-melting Mg-Al-Si or Mg-Cr-Si eutectics at 850–900 °C.
The transient liquid accelerates atomic diffusion and wets grain boundaries, thereby improving densification.
Transient-liquid processing suppresses Laves phases and Cr-V-rich precipitates by kinetically trapping a disordered BCC solid solution.
The 850–900 °C window supplies enough thermal energy for BCC-matrix nucleation and liquid flow while remaining below the onset of dominant Mg volatility.
Mixing energetics in Cr-V/W-Ta systems are associated with Cr-V segregation and precipitate formation.
Suppressing chemical ordering in the selected temperature window prevents jagged phase boundaries and the embrittlement associated with a ductile-brittle-ductile transition.
Sintering at 850–900 °C will produce greater than 95% theoretical density.
The optimized material will have a homogeneous, single-phase-like BCC microstructure with minimal residual porosity.
Al and Cr will form protective Al2O3 and Cr2O3 surface layers that improve oxidation or corrosion resistance.
The 850–900 °C product will have better oxidation resistance and mechanical properties than products sintered at 800 °C or 1000 °C.
Standard sintering at 800 °C gives insufficient densification and high porosity.
Sintering at 1000 °C causes excessive Mg loss, brittle Laves phases, Cr-V-rich precipitates, and coarse dendritic segregation.
Below 800 °C, relative density falls below 90% because diffusion is insufficient.
Above 1000 °C, Mg volatility and severe elemental segregation occur, destabilizing the BCC matrix and promoting Laves precipitation.
Brittle C14 Laves phases increase cracking tendency and deteriorate alloy properties.

contradictions.description: The specified and experimentally proposed Mg-Nb-Mo-Cr-Al-Si mixture contains no V, yet suppression and measurement of Cr-V-rich precipitates are central to the hypothesis and falsification criteria.
